experimental_method: Quasi-static analytic method: 35 cm3 sapphire-window cell with a recirculation pump; vapour and liquid phases (and, with the cell tilted, the CO2-rich liquid) sampled by electronically actuated valves into a gas chromatograph (TCD for CO2 and H2O, FID for CH4) calibrated by an absolute method.
uncertainties_stated: u(T) = 0.05 K (PRT 0.01 K plus bath fluctuations); u(p) = 5 kPa; standard uncertainties of each mole fraction printed per cell (combined standard uncertainty, GUM, eq 8; loop-volume uncertainty excluded); u(x) from 1e-6 to 3e-3 depending on component and phase.
quality_remarks: (1) Table 5, T = 285.15 K, phase II at p = 5.529 MPa: printed u(x2) = 0.0058 while all neighbouring u(x2) of phase II are 0.0004-0.0014; probably a misprint for 0.00058, kept as printed. (2) Table 5, T = 290.15 K, phase III at 7.926 MPa: printed u(x1) = 0.000032 and u(x2) = 0.0016, about three times the neighbouring values; kept as printed. (3) Table 5 pressures are printed with 2 to 4 decimals (6.77, 7.72, 6.2782, 7.1595, 7.7265 ...); the III-phase pressure 7.1595 MPa is printed both at 295.15 K and at 297.65 K, and phases I and II share 7.1773 MPa at 297.65 K; kept as printed. (4) Table 5, 292.65 K, phase I at 7.803 MPa: x1 + x2 + x3 = 1.00015 (all other rows sum to 1 within 1e-4). (5) Table 8 (UCEP): phase II x3 (water in the CO2-rich liquid) is 6.9e-5 to 2.6e-4, 10 to 30 times smaller than phase II x3 of Table 5 at nearby T and p (1.8e-3 to 5.6e-3), while phase II x1 + x2 = 0.9998-1.0000; the trend of x3 with T (rising) also differs from the Table 5 values; the Table 8 phase II water fraction may be a misprint or a column shift, kept as printed and flagged in mapping_8b. (6) Table 6, phase II at the lowest pressure of each isotherm has large water fractions (0.0658 at 373.15 K and 2.009 MPa; 0.3445 at 423.15 K and 2.102 MPa); physically plausible near the water vapour pressure, kept. (7) The CO2:CH4 ratio of the two-phase VLE gas was held near 1:1 (text says 'molar ratio ... about 0.5', meaning y1 ~ y2 ~ 0.5). (8) Component numbering differs between tables: Table 4 has 1 = CO2, 2 = H2O; Tables 5, 6, 8 have 1 = CH4, 2 = CO2, 3 = H2O.
supporting_information: Only the main PDF is available. The paper's measured tables (4, 5, 6, 7, 8) are all printed in the main text; the text does not refer to measured data being in Supporting Information.
